*PharmaCraft Daily - 02 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Respiratory)
Q: Salbutamol relieves acute asthma by acting as a?
Ans: Beta-2 agonist
Why: Salbutamol is a short-acting beta-2 agonist (SABA) causing bronchodilation - the reliever of choice.

🌍 *FMGE* (Respiratory)
Q: The reliever of choice in an acute asthma attack is inhaled?
Ans: Salbutamol
Why: Inhaled salbutamol (SABA) gives rapid bronchodilation and is the reliever of choice in acute asthma.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Respiratory)
Q: Omalizumab is used in severe allergic asthma and targets?
Ans: Free IgE
Why: Omalizumab is an anti-IgE monoclonal antibody reducing allergic asthma exacerbations.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Respiratory)
Q: Why can non-selective beta-blockers be dangerous in asthma even if cardioselective seems safer?
Ans: Beta-2 blockade can trigger bronchoconstriction
Why: Beta-2 blockade removes bronchodilator tone; even cardioselective agents lose selectivity at higher doses.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper II: Clinical Pharmacology)
Q: Phase III trials are primarily designed to establish?
Ans: Confirmatory efficacy and safety in large populations
Why: Phase III randomised controlled trials confirm efficacy and monitor adverse effects in large patient groups.
